instructions: Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes and dice the onion.
Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp salt and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until it's soft and golden.
Stir in the cumin and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Add the potatoes, 1/2 tsp salt and 2 tbsp water. Stir, then cover and turn the heat to medium low. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until a knife slides into a potato easily.
Beat the eggs in a bowl with the pepper and a pinch of salt. Pour them over the potatoes and cover the pan for 2 minutes.
Uncover and stir gently until the eggs are just set. Take the pan off the heat. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Sprinkle with the parsley and serve with pickles and olives.
To pack, let it cool and keep it in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Eat it at room temperature or warm it in a skillet over low heat.
method_notes: No version with enough ratings was found, so this follows SBS Food (Patrick Abboud): onion and potatoes cooked covered until soft, then beaten eggs stirred through. A Cedar Spoon and Tara's Multicultural Table agree on the method; Tara's caramelizes the onion for 20 to 30 minutes, which is too slow for a lunch, and uses olive oil and cumin. Ghee is swapped for olive oil to keep it dairy-free, and the flatbread is left off so it stays gluten-free.
